title: Royalway Space Rental Platform
description: Built a full-stack venue-rental booking platform for Royalway Christian Centre's private event hall in Ellicott City, MD, with the Next.js App Router, MySQL for persistent reservations, and Stripe for deposits and payment collection. Implemented an interactive layout visualizer for theater, round-table, and open-floor setups, a real-time pricing calculator, Zod-validated booking forms, and automated confirmation emails via Nodemailer. Live and processing real venue bookings.

star.situation: Royalway Christian Centre was booking their private event hall in Ellicott City by phone and email, with no way for people to see pricing or layouts online.
star.task: Build a booking platform that could take real deposits, show pricing for different room setups, and confirm bookings automatically.
star.action: Built it solo with the Next.js App Router and MySQL for reservations, added Stripe for deposits and payment collection, an interactive layout visualizer for theater, round-table, and open-floor setups, a real-time pricing calculator, Zod-validated booking forms, and automated confirmation emails through Nodemailer.

title: Adisah African Store
description: Website and WhatsApp ordering flow for Adisah African Store, an African grocer in Upper Marlboro, MD. Customers build their grocery list on the site and send it straight to WhatsApp, and a redirect-based QR system collects Google reviews without ever needing reprinting.

star.situation: A Maryland African grocer wanted a real website instead of just a flyer and word of mouth, with ordering that matched how their customers already order: a phone call or a WhatsApp message.
star.task: Build a site from a photo of their flyer as the only source material, ship real ordering and review flows with it, and set up the SEO and analytics a new small-business domain needs from day one.
star.action: Built it with Next.js 16 and Tailwind, with every store detail (hours, address, categories) in one data file so it's easy to correct as the owner confirms more of it. The order page lets a customer build a grocery list and sends it straight into a WhatsApp message instead of a cart and checkout flow nobody running a corner store wants to maintain. Printed review cards point at a short redirect route rather than Google directly, so the QR code never needs reprinting if the review link changes. Added LocalBusiness structured data, a Google Analytics 4 property with key events, and a verified Search Console property, then registered the domain and put the whole thing on Railway with HTTPS.
star.result: Live at adisahafricanstore.com since October 2026, with real orders going out over WhatsApp while the owner works through the product photos and details still pending confirmation.

title: Jigzack Cleaning Services Platform
description: Live platform for Jigzack Cleaning Services, a LAWMA-approved waste collection company serving Lagos and Port Harcourt. It combines the public website with customer, employee and admin dashboards. Pickup schedules and monthly invoices are generated automatically from each customer's pickup frequency and property details, and every pickup is backed by before and after photos.

star.situation: Jigzack Cleaning Services, a LAWMA-approved waste collection company in Lagos and Port Harcourt, was running customer signup, pickup scheduling, billing and payments by hand, with no system behind any of it.
star.task: Build one platform for three very different users: customers who want a clear record of pickups and invoices, employees out on the route, and admins who approve accounts and run the business. None of them could be allowed to see data that isn't theirs.
star.action: Built it with Next.js 16 and Supabase and put it on Railway behind the company's own domain. The database has 12 tables and 61 row level security policies, so access control lives in Postgres and the public API key can't read or change anything it shouldn't. Before launch I audited function permissions and revoked public access to the ones that exposed admin data. Customers sign up, confirm their email, submit property details and wait for approval. Employees join by invite, see their assigned pickups, run a timer and upload before and after photos, compressed in the browser so phone photos don't fail. Apartment estates are modeled as a customer account with a units table underneath, so each tenant gets a login against one shared invoice. A parser turns free-text answers like "twice a week" into concrete dates, and anything it can't read defaults to weekly and is flagged for an admin. A daily GitHub Actions job keeps pickups scheduled four weeks ahead and creates each month's invoices on the 1st, using per-unit pricing that skips vacant units. The app also sends realtime notifications, generates invoice and receipt PDFs, emails through Resend and publishes structured data for search.
star.result: It's live at jigzackcleaningservices.com, with signup, approvals, scheduling, invoicing and payments handled in one system instead of by hand. The repository has 63 commits since December 2025.
